1. **Assessment & planning:** Inventory the 2 TB PostgreSQL instance (version, extensions, schema objects, replication/logical decoding support), size the target managed service (compute, storage, IOPS, PG version parity), and set success criteria (max downtime ≤2 hours, zero data loss, verified integrity).

2. **Provision & configure target:** Stand up the managed cloud PostgreSQL instance, match extensions/parameters to the source, configure networking/VPC peering or VPN, security groups, IAM, and encryption at rest/in transit.

3. **Set up continuous replication:** Configure logical replication (or a native migration/CDC tool such as pglogical, AWS DMS, or a similar managed replication service) from on-prem to the cloud target so the bulk of the 2 TB can sync ahead of cutover without blocking production.

4. **Rehearsal on non-production data:** Take a full backup/clone of production, restore it to a staging copy of the target service, and perform a full dry-run migration and cutover rehearsal (including replication catch-up, application reconfiguration, and rollback) to measure timing and surface issues before touching production.

5. **Stakeholder communication (pre-migration):** Notify all ~4,000 daily active users and internal stakeholders of the scheduled Sunday maintenance window, expected impact, and a status-update channel; confirm on-call staffing for the migration.

6. **Pre-cutover full backup:** Immediately before the maintenance window, take a full verified backup (and confirm restorability) of the production database — this is the mandatory backup preceding any destructive/modifying step.

7. **Begin maintenance window — freeze writes:** Put the application into read-only/maintenance mode, stop write traffic to on-prem PostgreSQL, and let replication fully drain to the cloud target.

8. **Final sync & cutover:** Confirm replication lag is zero, stop replication, update application connection strings/DNS/secrets to point at the managed cloud database, and bring the application back online.

9. **Data integrity verification:** Run row-count comparisons, checksums (e.g., `pg_checksums`/table hash comparisons), and key business-metric spot checks between source and target before declaring success; hold the maintenance window open until verification passes.

10. **Go-live validation & monitoring:** Run smoke tests/critical transactions against the live application on the new database, monitor performance, error rates, and replication/connection health closely for the first hours.

11. **Rollback procedure (contingency):** If integrity checks fail, cutover exceeds the window, or critical errors appear, revert DNS/connection strings back to on-prem PostgreSQL (kept fully intact and untouched as the fallback), resume write traffic there, and restore from the pre-cutover backup (step 6) if any on-prem data was altered; communicate the rollback to stakeholders and reschedule.

12. **Post-migration wrap-up & communication:** Notify stakeholders/users of successful completion (or rollback), decommission or archive the on-prem database only after a defined retention/verification period, and document lessons learned.

STEP COUNT: 12
